diagnoses.summary: Abnormal PCA with both T2 and SPE violated; strongest evidence points to an upset causing a large coherent shift, most consistent with overheating of the CSTR that drives reaction and pressure increase.

Both Hotelling T² and SPE are violated with a large, coherent upset dominated by the CSTR temperature rise and reactor pressure signals. The strongest rule-based indication is an actuator fault at the CSTR heater causing heater command/actual mismatch and elevated temperature, consistent with the alarm on cstr_temperature_K.

PCA signals a large, coherent plant upset with both T2 and SPE violations. The strongest indicators point to the CSTR heater acting abnormally, causing a temperature rise that triggers high-temperature alarms and drives the control loop R_TIC to saturate. Sensor/controller disagreement also present. Likely multiple issues, but reactor heater fault is primary.

PCA shows a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violations, dominated by a single measurement/controller interaction. The SPE is largely explained by the R_TIC channel, pointing to a sensor/measurement issue in the TIC loop rather than a pure process disturbance.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violated, dominated by reactor temperature rise with the CSTR heater control loop saturated. This points to an actuator fault in the CSTR heater or its control action being unable to remove the heat effectively.

PCA flags a large, coherent process upset dominated by reactor temperature in the CSTR with simultaneous SPE violation, alarms on cstr_temperature_K, and a saturated TIC loop. This points to a reactor temperature upset driven by an actuator fault at the CSTR heater or a fast degradation of reaction rate, with heater fault being most likely given the evidence of high temperature alarms and heater-related SIF tendencies.

Abnormal PCA with large coherent upset in the CSTR temperature/pressure region, with reactor temperature loop (R_TIC) saturated and an active alarm (R_T_H). Likely a heater fault causing overheating, with possible catalyst/activity issues contributing to elevated temperature.

PCA abnormal; likely H2 PCV related fault affecting reactor pressure control. High T2 and high SPE with cstr_pressure_bar as the dominant contributor point to a PCV/pressure issue rather than a pure sensor drift.

PCA signals a large, coherent upset with strong contribution from CSTR pressure measurement; likely H2 vent (PCV) related fault propagating to reactor pressure. No alarms/trips yet, but pressure headed toward high limits while controller acts to compensate.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset centered on the CSTR with strong heating influence and reactor pressure signaling. The most likely cause is a fault in the CSTR heater acting at high output, with secondary contributions from H2 PCV related faults.

PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset with both T² and SPE violated. The strongest evidence points to an abnormal heating of the CSTR core, with temperature driving upward and heater controller under limitations. Upstream signals (temperature driven) align with a faulty CSTR heater command/response.
Abnormal PCA with large coherent upset dominated by CSTR temperature rise driven by heater action; high SPE indicates a sensor/actuator-driven upset with compensating loop activity.

The abnormal PCA readout is dominated by a coherent shift with strong SPE caused primarily by a faulty measurement, with a possible accompanying actuator fault. The most likely single fault is a sensor fault on the reactor temperature indicator (op.R_TIC). A secondary plausible fault is reactor heater output behaving abnormally (reactor_heater_stuck_high).

PCA indicates a large, coherent process movement with simultaneous SPE violation. The dominant driver is the reactor temperature sensor together with the R_TIC control signal, consistent with a sensor fault on R_TIC driving the apparent temperature upset.

PCA shows a large, coherent plant upset with both T² and SPE violations, dominated by CSTR temperature rise and heater/controller interaction. The rule-based evidence points to a stuck/high heater tendency and possible catalyst activity effects contributing to the abnormal CSTR temperature rise.
PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violations. The strongest evidence points to a CSTR heater fault causing elevated reactor temperature and related process changes.

PCA monitor detects a large coherent upset with both T2 and SPE violations. The strongest rule-based hypothesis points to an actuator fault in the CSTR heater, with catalyst activity loss as a plausible secondary contributor.

The PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with significant temperature rise in the CSTR coupled with abnormal heater control action. The fixed-rule hypotheses point to a stuck-high CSTR heater as the dominant fault.
Most likely an actuator fault related to the CSTR heater causing a heater command–actual mismatch and excessive reactor temperature.

The PCA detects a large, coherent plant upset with both T² and SPE violations, dominated by a rise in CSTR temperature with the reactor heater/casual control activity implicated. Likely a stuck/high heater output causing elevated reactor temperature, with secondary contributions from catalyst activity changes.
PCA flags a large, coherent upset with concurrent high T2 and high SPE; most likely a heater-related fault driving a reactor temperature upset, with possible catalyst effects.

Abnormal PCA with large coherent upset (high T² and high SPE) dominated by reactor temperature rise with corresponding heater control action. Most likely an actuator fault causing excessive heat input.

PCA indicates a large, coherent upset with both T² and SPE violated. Most likely the reactor heater actuator is stuck high, causing an elevated CSTR temperature and driving the TIC reading contributions.
